_comment: gateway-upstream-routing (REQ-UPRT-001..003): an api endpoint may carry several targets, chosen by a rule on the request, by weight, or by a stable hash of the consumer when sticky, and skipped while their source's circuit breaker is open. Without targets an endpoint uses its one targetId as before. The call log records which target served a call and why; callsPerTarget counts calls per target for the endpoint page.

targets.title: Targets
targets.description: Sources this api endpoint routes to. When set and non-empty it replaces targetId. A target with a `when` rule (JsonLogic over parameters, headers and the JSON body) is used when the rule matches, together with the other targets of its group; targets without a rule form the default group. Within a group the target is picked by weight.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: Share of the group's calls, relative to the other targets; 95 and 5 send about one call in twenty to the second.

when.title: Rule
when.description: JsonLogic rule over parameters, headers and body; empty for the default group.

group.title: Group
group.description: Name shared by targets with a rule that split the same traffic; a target with a rule and no group is a group of its own.

sticky.title: Sticky
sticky.description: Keep each consumer on the same target while the weights and the healthy targets stay the same. With few consumers this unbalances the weights.

routedTarget.title: Routed target
routedTarget.description: The source that served this call, for an endpoint with several targets.

routedReason.title: Routed reason
routedReason.description: Why that target was chosen: rule:<index>, weight, sticky or retry.
